boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Pine Bluff record (October 25, 1863) in Advance on Little Rock [September-October 1863]. Caldwell's pursuit of Marmaduke is context. The freedmen who built and defended the cotton-bale works are recorded as reported. Campaign-wide marches, returns and multi-action loss totals are context; they are not assigned to one record or added across records. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. The frozen side-specific numerical strength bounds are blank (missing_numeric_strength). No figure in this pass is adopted as a simultaneous opening force.

claims.value: The frozen force field reads Pine Bluff Garrison (two under-strength cavalry regiments and a company of state militia) [US] and division [CS], with no numerical bounds; the live field reads zero. Clayton says his force amounted to some 550 men, that prisoners put Marmaduke at 2,000 to 3,000 with twelve guns and he thought about 2,500, and that his force held off four times its number. Marmaduke says the garrison's effective force was about 600 with seven guns. NPS calls the 300 men who rolled out cotton bales African-American soldiers; Clayton and Talbot describe them as freedmen from the contraband camp, fifteen of whom had arms.
claims.rationale: Interested own-strength and enemy figures; the NPS 'soldiers' is not supported by the inspected reports. None is adopted as a matched opening strength. The live zero is not measured absence.

claims.value: Clayton says that within half an hour he had barricaded every street into the court square with cotton bales, planted his guns to command each street and posted sharpshooters in the buildings on the square; Talbot says a further breastwork was built under the river bank. Marmaduke says he held the whole town except the court-house and yard, fortified by heavy cotton-bale breastworks.
claims.rationale: Works described by interested reports. They were improvised on the morning of the attack on Clayton's order, hence the commander-created tag; this is a hypothesis about timing and agency, not a causal estimate.

Marmaduke and Colonel Powell Clayton; the live page lists Marmaduke without a rank.

claims.value: The frozen result reads Union victory and the live result Union Victory. Clayton says the enemy retreated about 2 p.m., leaving many dead and wounded, and he followed for a mile. Marmaduke says he withdrew because the works could only be stormed at too high a cost. NPS says the Confederates retired, leaving Pine Bluff to the Federals.
claims.rationale: Retain the original result and engagement interval; later movements and campaign contribution are different measures. No new probabilities or individual causal credit.

claims.value: The frozen casualty text reads Total unknown (US 56; CS unknown); the live field reads 96 (US 56; CS 40). Clayton gives 11 killed, 27 wounded and 1 missing, plus 5 freedmen killed and 12 wounded (Talbot gives the same 5 and 12); these printed components sum to 56. He estimates the enemy's killed and wounded at about 130, probably 150, holds 33 prisoners, 15 of them wounded, and says Marmaduke burned some of his own wounded to death in the fires. Marmaduke gives his own loss as about 40 killed and wounded. The compiled Union return is garbled in OCR.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap. Whether the frozen US 56 includes the freedmen is not established; the freedmen are recorded, not merged with military casualties.

open_questions: Steele's transmittal (No. 1, read at its opening), Pace's, Scudder's and Clark's reports (Nos. 3-5), Caldwell's pursuit report (No. 6) and the Confederate brigade and division reports (Nos. 8-16) remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC is one family. Davidson's September 12, 1863 report and Price's November 20, 1863 report with his November 25 letter are separate author families for Bayou Fourche; Clayton's October 27, 1863 report and Marmaduke's October 26 report are separate author families for Pine Bluff. All are interested participant accounts. Talbot's inclosure and the compiled casualty returns (garbled in OCR) are not counted as further families. No retrospective history covering these actions was inspected; the first-pass effort stayed with NPS/CWSAC and two report families per record. Official Records Series I, Volume XXII, Part 1 is a shared container, not an additional witness. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
